text:
miguel: pagerduty: CRITICAL - model-catalog-service: high error rate detected for model-serving v3-rev42 (seq mismatch)
incident-bot: page fired to @oncall-sre, 1/5 escalation policy
miguel: seeing spikes from US-east customers, a subset of requests returning 500 with 'sequence_id mismatch'
sara: can you paste the logs?
miguel: tail from prod (redacted):
```
2024-11-17T10:02:11Z ERROR handler: request_id=abc123 model=v3-rev42 error="sequence_id out of order" input_seq=12 kv_last_seq=11
2024-11-17T10:02:12Z ERROR handler: request_id=def456 model=v3-rev42 error="tokenizer mismatch: unknown start_token"
```
jessica: that tokenizer error smells like a revision that changed tokenizer metadata but catalog still pointed at previous tokenizer mapping
miguel: confirms: catalog entry for v3-rev42 references tokenizer:v2.0 but the artifact in model-store has tokenizer:v2.1 (sequence encoding changed)
sara: impact? percent of traffic and customers affected?
miguel: about 2.7% of gen traffic in us-east, concentrated on customers that pinned to v3 (no fallback). A few high-throughput tenants hit it and saw elevated 500s and increased latency
incident-bot: pagerduty: acknowledged by miguel
jessica: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback catalog pointer to v3-rev41 (old revision) 2) deploy tokenizer compatibility shim (risky) 3) route traffic to replica in eu-west (latency cost)
sara: rollback sounds fastest. can we atomically repoint catalog? any migrations needed?
miguel: catalog patch is atomic and supports canary. I can promote v3-rev41 with immediate route override. prepping rollback now
jessica: notify Platform API so long-lived pinned routes from customers aren't silently broken when we change pointer
miguel: running command: `./catalogctl promote --model v3 --from rev41 --to default --reason "hotfix: tokenizer mismatch" --no-automatic-rollout`
sara: heads-up to support: can we confirm customer impact list and message?__@support__ ping
incident-bot: deploy-bot: catalog change queued, canary=10% -> starting
miguel: canary reports look good, no sequence errors after canary hits rev41
jessica: start rolling to 100%, keep close watch on error-rate and latency metrics
miguel: rolling to 100% now
incident-bot: change applied: catalog default for v3 now points to rev41 (rolled out at 2024-11-17T10:11:45Z)
sara: confirm metrics: error-rate back to baseline, 500s down from 3.2% to 0.1% in us-east
jessica: excellent. action items: - keep rev42 in quarantine, do not promote until tokenizer metadata reconciled - run a tokenization regression test suite against rev42 artifacts - add a pre-promotion check in CI to validate tokenizer version matches catalog mapping
miguel: documenting customer-impact: affected customers: cust-alpha (90m downtime window with elevated 500s), cust-beta (partial errors, feature degradation). Support to triage crediting and outbound comms
sara: i'll create an incident summary and notify legal for any SLA considerations. assign RCA owners? jessica for model-onboarding checks, miguel for catalog tooling and automation
jessica: will add CI preflight and a warning flag when tokenizer ABI differs
incident-bot: pagerduty: incident closed by miguel at 2024-11-17T10:20:30Z
miguel: adding final notes: root cause = model artifact pushed with tokenizer v2.1 but catalog mapping not updated; missing pre-promotion validation allowed rev42 to become default for some routes. next steps: quarantine rev42, backfill catalog validation, postmortem + timeline, support outreach
sara: thanks everyone, good rapid rollback. follow-up doc in #incidents with timeline and customer comms draft
support: acknowledged, we'll prepare outreach and crediting proposals
jessica: leaving a small TODO: add a continuous monitor for tokenizer-version drift across model-store vs catalog
miguel: proposing a quick patch to catalogctl to reject promotions when tokenizer mismatch detected. I'll open PR and link to postmortem
sara: if no objections, i'll mark this as mitigated and schedule RCA sync tomorrow 09:00 PT
miguel: ack
jessica: ack :thumbsup:
